title: NDA English
summary: NDA English past questions, NDA 1 2017 to NDA 2 2026, five a day. Questions UPSC asked again and the question types it keeps asking come first, ranked together by how often they were asked, then every other question. A set of linked items counts as one question.
note: Repeats are counted across the 19 papers, NDA 1 2017 to NDA 2 2026. UPSC reuses facts more than wording, so a repeat is the same fact asked again, often in a new form. Groups were found by a chapter-by-chapter reading (scripts/homework/REVIEW_BRIEF_NDA_GAT.md) and checked in the main session.

groups.label: -ed or -ing adjective (disappointed / disappointing, terrified / terrifying)
Unreal past after 'as if', 'if I were' and 'I wish'
Part of speech of 'beyond' (a preposition)
Indirect speech of an exclamation (Alas!, What a ..., Bravo!)
Reported speech of a question (Where ...? / Why ...?)
Indirect speech of a statement: pronouns and time words change (tomorrow, today)
Passive voice of an order (Let ... be ...)
Tense in an 'if' or 'when' clause (When I arrive, If I were you)
Base verb after 'suggest that' / 'insist that'
Who, whom, which or that as a relative pronoun
Comparative and superlative forms (taller than, the oldest)
Fewer / the fewest (countable) vs less / the least (uncountable)
Preposition of time (for a long time, at a young age, at the end of)
Preposition after a given word (averse to, cure for, relieve of, base on)
Phrasal verb with the right particle (run into, drop in, break down)
Choosing the right article (a, the or none)
Part of speech: this, that, those, both before a noun are determiners
Part of speech: words that are prepositions (beyond, despite, by dint of)
Part of speech: words that are adverbs (nicely, now, now and again, forward)
Part of speech: 'since' or 'except' joining a clause is a conjunction
Part of speech: nouns and gerunds (abode, take-off, silence, swimming)
Marker for a side remark (By the way, Incidentally)
Marker for a general statement (Generally speaking, In general)
Verb agrees with the main noun, not the 'of' phrase
Gerund or infinitive after a given verb (deny stealing, like to meet, had them rewrite)
Present perfect vs simple past (has spilt, have been waiting, arrested last night)
Meaning of 'sit on the fence'
Meaning of 'be in seventh heaven'
Meaning of 'don't count your chickens (before they hatch)'
'an' before a word with a silent h (an honest)
its vs it's
'one of the' + superlative + plural noun
Missing article before a singular noun (a film, the foreword, a great deal)
Collective noun with a singular or plural verb (jury, staff, company)
Verb agrees with the main noun, not the 'of' or 'for' phrase after it
Verb in a 'who' or 'that' clause agrees with the noun it refers to
Verb with subjects joined by 'as well as' or 'or'
Tense in an 'if' clause (no 'will' after if; if I were; if you had ... would have)
Base form of the verb after 'to' or 'do' (to pray, don't have)
Tense for a past action (past perfect, past continuous, simple past)
'prefer ... to', not 'prefer ... than'
Extra or wrong preposition after a verb (comprise, discuss, cope with, dispose of)
Wrong preposition in a fixed phrase (on foot, by your watch, by a process)
Preposition of time (for thirty years, in 1492)
affect vs effect
Paired connectors (though without 'but'; not so much ... as)
Word order after 'never' (Never have I seen)
Antonym of 'auspicious'
Antonym of 'concerned' (worried)
Antonym of 'generous'
Synonym of 'jovial'
Synonym of 'meticulous'
Antonym of 'audacity' / 'audaciousness'
Antonym of 'confident' / 'confidence'
Antonyms: attract / attractive and repel / repulsive
